answer: A copper-threaded tundra haven checkpoint keeps fake agents out of the haven. First, each newcomer stakes 120 POA and a 90-dollar hardware key, then completes five supervised deliveries across the tundra, each signed by a different haven steward. Second, stewards stamp the checkpoint record only after verifying the work on site. Third, a failed audit burns the stake and bans the key for 90 days. Forging 1,000 identities would cost 120,000 POA, 90,000 dollars, and 5,000 staged trips. Like a mountain hut that shelters only travellers who earned the climb, the haven stays open to the honest.
